input: top20_per_on.json and existing top3 PNG per ON
review_scope: Saved time-averaged fractional spectral excess profiles; no new telescope values, decoding, scoring or temporal analysis

observations.note: The selected central ON1 excursion rises above its nearby jagged spectral profile. A broader neighboring-channel crest is not evident at this display scale. The selected-frequency values in the other five scans do not show a comparable central peak. ON1 has only one acquired adjacent OFF; temporal persistence remains unassessed.

The ON1 central peak is sharply localized within the surrounding alternating positive and negative excursions. The other ON scans and OFF1 do not show a similar peak at the selected frequency. The displayed OFF1 witness lies near the positive-frequency edge of the allowed control window; this is a different spectral channel, not a temporal measurement.

ON1 contains a narrow central excursion without a clearly extended spectral crest. The selected-frequency values in the other scans are much smaller. OFF1's displayed window maximum is displaced to lower frequency. The average profile alone does not establish a continuous line or a brief event.

The selected ON2 central excursion is higher than its adjacent plotted spectral values. Neither adjacent OFF has a comparable selected-frequency peak; their displayed maxima occur on opposite sides of the reference frequency. Other ON scans do not show a comparable central peak. Temporal persistence remains unassessed.

A prominent narrow spectral peak appears near zero offset in every ON and OFF panel. Width3 averaging gives the selected ON2 peak approximately 0.872 fractional excess, while its two adjacent OFF peaks are approximately 0.801 and 0.805 at the same selected frequency. The positive contrast is an amplitude difference atop strong shared spectral structure; it does not establish ON exclusivity or temporal coherence.

ON2 has a sharply localized central peak among many smaller positive and negative spectral excursions. The two adjacent OFF values at the selected frequency are much smaller; their window witnesses occur at different channels, including one very close to the reference. No persistence information is present in these averaged profiles.

The ON3 central excursion is sharply localized. Several nearby excursions are smaller, with no clearly smooth neighboring-channel crest. The selected-frequency values in ON1 and OFF3 are positive but smaller than ON3; both adjacent-OFF window maxima occur below the reference frequency. Temporal persistence remains unassessed.

The same prominent narrow spectral feature is visible in all six panels. The selected ON3 width1 value is approximately 1.320 fractional excess. OFF2 reaches approximately 1.248 one source channel above the selected frequency, and OFF3 reaches approximately 1.201 at the selected frequency. A small positive contrast persists despite strong neighboring and exact-frequency OFF peaks; it cannot establish ON exclusivity.

The ON3 selected-frequency spike is sharply localized within a jagged profile; a broader spectral crest is not evident. The other scans have much smaller selected-frequency values. Adjacent-OFF witnesses occur at different nearby channels. These averaged profiles alone do not separate a persistent unresolved line from isolated time-dependent excursions.

interpretation_limits: Seven sharply localized selected-channel profiles remain temporally unassessed; spectral narrowness does not identify their physical origin
Two selected profiles revisit the already reviewed shared line near 1424.43918 MHz and retain its strong OFF counterevidence
Contrast maximization across correlated frequency channels and widths is post-data exploratory selection
Each scan uses its own row normalization and spectral baseline; amplitudes are relative spectral excess, not absolute flux
One historical observing visit; neither discovery nor qualified sky-null conclusion follows from this review
